collection.description: A villager has been the healers' apprentice for a year.

ask.text:
(subject) has been the healers' apprentice for a year. (subject.He/She) has fetched water, ground roots, and watched. Today, for the first time, (healer), the head healer, has gone to the far side of the island for a birth, and left (subject) in charge. And today, of course, (friend) has come in burning with fever and covered in spots.
(subject) has two ideas. (subject.He/She) can do exactly what (healer) would do: bitter bark tea, cool cloths, wait. Or (subject.he/she) can try the thing (subject.he/she) has been reading about in the old scrolls, a paste of crushed moss that (healer) says is "old nonsense."
Should (subject) do it (healer)'s way, or try the moss?

c1o1.text: The fever breaks at midnight. By morning the spots are fading. When (healer) gets back, (subject.he/she) looks at (friend), and at (subject), and nods once. That's all. It is the proudest moment of (subject)'s life, and (subject.he/she) is a much better healer for having done it alone.

c1o2.text: It works, slowly, over three days. When (healer) comes back, (subject) tells (subject.him/her) everything, and (healer) asks so many questions that by the end of it they are both teaching the other healers what they found out. The healers' hut is a busier place after that.

c1.text: (subject) brews the bitter bark tea exactly as (subject.he/she) has watched (healer) brew it a hundred times, and lays the cool cloths on (friend)'s forehead, and waits...

c2o1.text: By evening the spots are gone, and the fever with them. (subject) puts the paste on everyone else in the village who has a cough, a rash or a fever, and by the time (healer) gets back, nobody in the village is sick. (healer) looks at the moss for a long time. "Old nonsense," (subject.he/she) says at last. "I'll want to see the scroll."

c2o2.text: The moss makes the spots much worse. (friend)'s whole skin comes up in a red, itching rash on top of the fever. (subject) washes it off in a panic and does it (healer)'s way, and (friend) gets better, slowly, over a week. When (healer) gets back, (subject.he/she) doesn't say anything at all, which is worse than anything (subject.he/she) could have said.

c2.text: (subject) crushes the moss into a green paste and spreads it on (friend)'s spots, feeling (subject.his/her) heart pound. (friend) says it smells like a wet dog...
